title: PostHog Pricing 2026 – Which Plan Fits Your Team?
summary: PostHog pricing tiers range from free to enterprise options. Compare plans to find the right fit for your team's analytics needs.
body_markdown:
## Frequently asked questions


Is PostHog really free? Yes, up to a monthly allowance on each product, and you pay only for usage beyond it.


The allowance resets every month and unused amounts don't carry forward, so a quiet month earns you no credit against a busy one. Treat the free tier as a monthly threshold, not a balance.


Does PostHog charge per seat or per user? No, team size doesn't change the price; usage does. Adding a colleague costs nothing, but that colleague's dashboards, replays and experiments generate events, and events are what you're billed for.


Compare this with seat-based tools, where a hire raises the bill the day they join. Here the bill moves only when your volume does.


### How do I stop PostHog bills from spiking?


Set a billing limit on each product, then cut the events you don't need. A limit caps spend at a figure you choose, and once you reach it PostHog stops ingesting that product's data until the next cycle.


So a cap protects your budget but can leave a gap. Set it above your normal usage and alert on it before you hit it.


Then trim at the source: drop noisy events, sample session recordings, and avoid autocapturing everything on high-traffic pages. The cap is a safety net, and volume control is what keeps the bill low.


### Does PostHog offer startup or nonprofit discounts?


If you're a startup, you can get credits that offset usage charges through a PostHog program, and eligibility rules are set in its docs. I can't confirm a nonprofit program from the material here, so check PostHog's current pricing and program pages before assuming one.


Either way, the free allowance already covers a small team. A discount matters only once your volume outgrows it.


### Can I self-host PostHog to avoid usage fees?


If you self-host the open-source version, PostHog's usage fees go away, but it's not free. You take on the servers, storage, upgrades and on-call time, and those costs grow with event volume just as the cloud bill would.


For a small project, that trade can work. For a team without spare engineering hours, the cloud plan with a billing limit is usually the cheaper line once you count labor. Price both before deciding.
